column3: “Heeds” in the first clause is not explicitly stated in Hebrew.
Hebrew says “eat good” and “soul”; BSB has “enjoys good things” and “desire.”
Hebrew names “soul” and “lips”; BSB has “life” and supplies “invites.”
Hebrew expressly names the slacker’s soul and says the diligent soul is “made fat,” not merely satisfied.
Hebrew explicitly names a lying word and uses an image of making foul; BSB has general falsehood and shame.
Hebrew expressly describes integrity of “way”; BSB has a man of integrity.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “rebuke” and explicitly “soul”; BSB has “threat” and “life.”
Hebrew makes the light “rejoice”; BSB says it “shines brightly.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says wealth “from vapor” and describes collecting by hand; BSB has dishonest wealth and hard work.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “word” and “fears a command”; BSB has “instruction” and “respects a command.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew identifies the faithful envoy as “healing”; BSB supplies the verb “brings.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew speaks of suffering harm; BSB has “will be destroyed.”
Hebrew uses an active verb for repaying the righteous with good; BSB makes prosperity their reward.
Hebrew says the sinner’s wealth is stored up for the righteous; BSB says it is passed to them.
Hebrew says “there is one swept away without justice”; BSB makes the food the subject of being swept away.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “satisfaction of his soul”; BSB has “heart’s content.” The wicked stomach lacks rather than being explicitly empty.
